cause.summary: The 128 false positives were not spurious detections. Every one was a detection of a real rendered cube whose visible-pixel centroid is more than 5 px from the projected 3D cube centre.
cause.label_bug: The dataset label computed 'visible' from the single projected-centre pixel. A cube whose centre is hidden behind a bin wall but whose top is rendered was therefore labelled invisible, even with hundreds of visible pixels. Fixed: visible = visible_pixels > 0, with centre_visible recorded separately.
cause.matching_bug: Precision and recall matched detections to the projected 3D centre only. Under partial occlusion the visible-pixel centroid must be offset, so a correct detection was scored as a false positive. Fixed: a detection inside the cube's visible bounding box matches that cube; pixel and 3D error remain measured only where the projected centre is unoccluded.

detector_change: none; the shipped detect_cubes is unchanged
note: The pinhole track has flat shading and exact material colours, so a corrected ground truth gives 100% detection. That is a logic check on the state machine and geometry, not evidence of camera perception quality. The RTX comparison in results/rtx_perception.json is the sim-to-sim measurement.
